label: Early-sequence <DEL> or t/x/c/q/3/y input (steps 2-5)
explanation: Never fires in the copy phase or at step 0. Fires only on inputs from a small token set: <DEL> (61% of activation mass; strongest, all top examples are <DEL> after a short L=3-4 sequence of letters like k,p,f,u,d,s,n) and the original-phase tokens t, x, c, q, 3, y (in that order of strength), almost always at their first occurrence. Magnitude and firing rate fall off with position: rate peaks at steps 2-5 and is near zero by step 8; <DEL> fires with precision 0.99 at L=3, 0.84 at L=4, 0.60 at L=5 and under 0.15 for L>=7. Trigger tokens that appear after an earlier trigger in the same sequence often stay silent, and <DEL> fires less after a trigger was seen, but that effect is only partial. Precision is about 0.5 because many in-window trigger tokens do not fire. Dev: P 0.51, R 0.81, F1 0.62, mass recall 0.88.
